Compromised @immobiliarelabs Backstage plugin on disk (binding.gyp + index.js / known hashes) AIDelivery Medium
Inventory/IOC detection for the trojanized @immobiliarelabs/backstage-plugin-gitlab(-backend) and backstage-plugin-ldap-auth(-backend) packages. Clean releases never shipped a binding.gyp, so the presence of binding.gyp or the 5 MB index.js inside those package paths — or any file matching the three published malicious SHA256s — confirms a compromised version was installed. Rationale: Built on the article's affected-package matrix plus the three published SHA256 IOCs; a binding.gyp inside these specific Backstage plugin directories is itself anomalous because the clean 2.1.1-era releases shipped neither binding.gyp nor a 5 MB index.js. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/immobiliarelabs-npm-packages-compromised • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/mal-2026-6527 • https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team intentionally staging the malicious tarball in an isolated analysis sandbox
  • A cached npm tarball retained on a build agent after remediation (already-known, low risk)
  • An offline mirror/proxy (Verdaccio/Artifactory) holding a quarantined copy for inspection
  • Hash collision is implausible — SHA256 matches are definitive
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the exact package@version from the path against the affected matrix (gitlab/gitlab-backend 3.0.3–7.0.2, 1.0.1, 2.1.2; ldap-auth(-backend) 1.1.3/1.1.4–5.2.1) and check whether node-gyp executed it (install actually ran). 2) Contain: pin/roll back to a known-clean version, purge the tarball from caches and lockfiles, isolate affected build agents, and rotate every credential reachable from that host/CI job. 3) Hunt: pivot to binding.gyp execution, Bun temp execution, IMDS access, and AI-assistant config writes on the same hosts; sweep the registry/repo org for republished (worm-propagated) packages from any maintainer account touched by these runners.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has "@immobiliarelabs" and (FolderPath has "backstage-plugin-gitlab" or FolderPath has "backstage-plugin-ldap-auth") and FileName in~ ("binding.gyp","index.js"))
    or SHA256 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108","da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707","ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath has "@immobiliarelabs" and (TargetFilePath has "backstage-plugin-gitlab" or TargetFilePath has "backstage-plugin-ldap-auth") and TargetFileName in~ ("binding.gyp","index.js"))
    or TargetFileSHA256 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108","da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707","ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")

   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children

status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.initial-access
logsource:

            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or SHA1 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or MD5 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or SHA1 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90") or MD5 in~ ("ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Jackson Maven typosquat C2 — beacon to fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82 AICommand & Control High
Hunts hosts resolving or connecting to the namespace-impersonation C2 (fasterxml.org / m.fasterxml.org) or the staging IP 103.127.243.82 used by the malicious org.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind artifact to pull a Cobalt Strike beacon. Article-specific: these are typosquats of the legitimate fasterxml.com / com.fasterxml namespace, so any hit is high-fidelity. Rationale: fasterxml.org / m.fasterxml.org and 103.127.243.82:8000 are the verbatim C2 from Aikido's analysis (config.txt + svchosts.exe staging), typosquatting the real fasterxml.com — so any resolution/connection is malicious by definition. Cross-checked Aikido and cybersecuritynews/SC Media. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-infiltrated-maven-central/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/maven-central-subjected-to-typosquatted-jackson-json-library
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox or researcher detonating the sample in-house
  • Threat-intel proxy / URL-crawler pre-resolving the IOC domain
  • DNS sinkhole or RPZ responding to the domain (benign, but worth confirming sink not real resolve)
  • Internal artifact-mirror health-check probing the coordinate's declared SCM/URL
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") // exclude analyst browser lookups of the IOC
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess (expect java.exe/javaw.exe from a Spring Boot app or CI runner); confirm whether the resolve led to an actual TCP connect to 103.127.243.82:8000 or :51211. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block fasterxml.org / m.fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82 at egress, and pull the build's dependency tree for org.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind. 3) Hunt: sweep all CI runners and dev machines that resolved org.fasterxml namespace coordinates, and pivot to UC2/UC3 for dropped svchosts.exe / payload.bin and the two SHA256 implants.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "fasterxml.org" or RemoteIP == "103.127.243.82"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery has "fasterxml.org" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DnsQuery, Kind = "dns", DstPort = int(null)),
(ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr == "103.127.243.82" or Url has "fasterxml.org" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Indicator = DstIpAddr, Kind = "net", DstPort = DstPortNumber)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Java/Spring drops & runs svchosts.exe (svchost masquerade) — Jackson typosquat implant AIInstallation High
Hunts the second-stage drop where the malicious JacksonSpringAutoConfiguration class writes payload.bin to temp and executes svchosts.exe (a typosquat of the legitimate svchost.exe). Article-specific via the exact filenames and the java.exe→svchosts.exe parent/child chain. Rationale: svchosts.exe (note trailing 's') is never a legitimate Windows binary and is the verbatim Windows payload name; pairing the java.exe parent with the two confirmed SHA256 implants makes this near-zero-FP. Sourced from Aikido's payload breakdown. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-infiltrated-maven-central/
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or pentester naming an unrelated test binary svchosts.exe
  • Red-team tooling intentionally masquerading as svchost
  • Unrelated commodity malware reusing the svchosts.exe name (still malicious — escalate)
  • EDR sample-replay / detonation lab running the captured artifact
Suppression filter
| where not(FolderPath has_any (@"\Tests\", @"\redteam\")) // suppress sanctioned test/red-team binaries
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the binary path (expect a temp/working dir, not System32) and parent (java.exe/javaw.exe from a Spring Boot app or CI build); validate SHA256 against the two known implant hashes. 2) Contain: kill the process, isolate the host, and quarantine svchosts.exe / payload.bin; block the C2 from UC1. 3) Hunt: search the host and peers for the hidden .idea.pid persistence marker, for beacons to 103.127.243.82:8000 / m.fasterxml.org:51211, and audit which builds resolved org.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "svchosts.exe"
   or SHA256 in ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f","702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has "svchosts.exe"
   or (ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe") and TargetProcessName has "svchosts.exe")

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Jackson typosquat Cobalt Strike implant hash sighting (Win + macOS/Linux) AIInstallation Medium
Vector-agnostic sweep for the two confirmed implant SHA256 hashes (svchosts.exe for Windows, 'update' for macOS/Linux) dropped by the malicious jackson-databind artifact. Catches the implant even when delivered outside the java→svchosts.exe chain (e.g. pulled directly into a CI cache). Rationale: The two SHA256 are the verbatim VirusTotal-confirmed Cobalt Strike beacons (Windows svchosts.exe + macOS/Linux 'update') from Aikido's IOC list; an exact-hash match is effectively zero-FP and covers non-Windows hosts the process/network UCs miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/maven-central-jackson-typosquatting-malware • https://www.scworld.com/brief/maven-central-subjected-to-typosquatted-jackson-json-library
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • EDR/AV quarantine copy of the same file retaining the original hash (benign artifact of detection)
  • Malware-research repository or sample-share host storing the IOC for analysis
  • Backup/forensic image containing a previously quarantined copy
  • Sandbox detonation lab re-fetching the sample
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","CSFalconService.exe") // exclude AV/EDR quarantine writes
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process and path — distinguish an AV/EDR quarantine vault (benign) from a live drop in a build/temp dir (true positive). 2) Contain: isolate the host, quarantine the file, and revoke any CI/cloud credentials reachable from the build that pulled jackson-databind (Cobalt Strike harvests CI secrets). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC1 (C2 to fasterxml.org / 103.127.243.82) and UC2 (svchosts.exe execution) on the same and neighbouring hosts, and inventory every repo/runner that resolved org.fasterxml.jackson.core coordinates.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f","702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f","702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd") or SHA1 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd") or MD5 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd") or SHA1 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd") or MD5 in~ ("8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["8bce95ebfb895537fec243e069d7193980361de9d916339906b11a14ffded94f", "702161756dfd150ad3c214fbf97ce98fdc960ea7b3970b5300702ed8c953cafd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental
description: |

    values. Use a watchlist or external indicator file for management
    at scale.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

tags:

    product: windows
detection:

        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA256=__HASH_PLACEHOLDER_REPLACE_ME__'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:

level: critical
